Accepted and applied: TSHR BBJ prior sensitivity stated in the abstract and the opening Discussion; PP.H3 added to Table 2 so the distinct-variant and unresolved readings rest on displayed numbers; the '81 comparisons crossed the 0.80 threshold' sentence rewritten as a classification statement with its 9x3x3 decomposition; per-locus variant counts (1,479-7,740) and the purpose of the BBJ-plus-FinnGen criterion stated in Methods; the reconstructed exposure unit defined as approximately one standard deviation; gene-specific 80% detection limits reported, showing the IGF1R estimate fell below its own limit in all three outcomes; 'modest IGF1R contribution' widened to 'inherited contribution' because the FinnGen CI reaches 2.33; MAPKAPK5 given three decimals in a footnote; the 1000 Genomes panel given its own citation (new reference 18, all later references renumbered). revision_note_20260915_eqtl_n: Methods now quantifies the eQTLGen per-variant sample size (median 28,092, range 232-31,684) instead of only 'up to 31,684'. Verified against Supplementary_Data_1_Instruments.csv: max n_samples is exactly 31,684, median 28,092, min 232; 27.4% of the 6,135 instruments have n < 20,000. Instrument strength is unaffected -- the P < 5e-8 selection threshold guarantees F >= 29.7 at any n -- and all instruments behind the reported backbone genes have n between 20,515 and 31,567 (F 33.0-375.0).
revision_note_20260915_methods: Methods reviewed line by line. References [8] and [11]-[24] each verified to resolve to the paper the sentence relies on. Three edits: (1) 'MR, colocalization and detectable effect sizes were compared (Tables S2-S3)' pointed at tables that hold MR estimates and detection limits but no colocalization -- the coloc frequency scenarios live only in Supplementary Data 3, and the sentence now says so; (2) the minimum F of 29.7 is now given against the conventional threshold of 10, so the number means something to a reader; (3) the two sentences on the reconstructed exposure scale merged into one without losing either fact (expression variance set to one; the genetic predictor is not standardized). The audit guard for that distinction matched one exact sentence and now accepts either voice while still failing if the distinction is dropped.
revision_note_20260915_results_p1: First Results paragraph reordered and de-duplicated. The abbreviation MHC was used one sentence before 'major histocompatibility complex (MHC)' defined it. Two sentences restated the Figure 1 legend almost verbatim ('each plotted point represents a gene-level MR result, not a single-SNP GWAS association' vs the legend's 'Each point represents one gene, not a SNP association'); the legend keeps that guidance and Results no longer repeats it. The 310-not-estimable caveat now follows the counts it derives from, and the composition of the 13 hits now follows the count of 13 instead of being separated from it. Verified: 5 of the 13 sit in the MHC (chr6:25-34 Mb; HLA-A, HLA-DQA2, C4A, TUBB, PSMB8) and 8 outside -- IFNGR1 is on chr6 but at 137 Mb -- so 'not confined to the MHC region' is accurate. 127 -> 116 words; no displayed value changed.
revision_note_20260915_results_tshr: TSHR Results paragraph tightened. It made the same point three times (UKB strong MR but no shared-variant support) and one of those sentences described Figure 2 rather than reporting a result. Merged to state it once and keep the interpretive takeaway. Two precision gains: the posteriors are now labelled 'under the primary prior' where they are first given, and UKB is identified as carrying the strongest MR association of the three outcomes (P = 8.77e-28 against 1.09e-14 BBJ and 2.82e-07 FinnGen, verified), which is what makes its non-colocalization worth reporting. 117 -> 98 words; no displayed value changed. Prior sensitivity was deliberately NOT repeated here -- the manuscript already states it in the Abstract, the Robustness subsection, the Discussion opening, the sensitivity paragraph, Limitations and Conclusions.
revision_note_20260915_results_igf1r: IGF1R Results: a 223-word single paragraph covering colocalization, alternative estimators, leave-one-out and the overall takeaway was split into colocalization (77 words) and MR sensitivity plus takeaway (175 words). One factual imprecision fixed: 'Each outcome also lost nominal significance under one other omission' read as all three outcomes, but FinnGen never reached nominal significance (full-set P = 0.182) and so had none to lose. Verified from the leave-one-out estimates: BBJ (full-set P = 0.0212) lost it under rs2654980 (0.0751) and rs59467480 (0.0503); UKB (0.0117) under rs2654980 (0.468) and rs117212126 (0.0529) -- two of four omissions in each of the two outcomes that reached P < 0.05. The text now says exactly that. Estimator claims re-verified: weighted median 0.0288 BBJ / 0.00244 UKB / 0.124 FinnGen; weighted mode 0.512 / 0.367 / 0.633.
revision_note_20260915_results_ctla4: CTLA4 Results: the takeaway ('the screen therefore recovered a known autoimmune association...') sat in the middle of the paragraph, ahead of the rs13030124 caveat that qualifies it, so a reader met the conclusion and then the reason to doubt it. Moved to the end and anchored to the arm it actually rests on -- BBJ, a single instrument, P = 5.45e-15 -- which the European two-SNP dependence does not touch. Added a Supplementary Methods pointer to the chromosome 16p11.2 one-regional-signal conclusion, whose LD (EAS r2 0.854/0.761/0.863) and GCTA-COJO evidence a reader could not otherwise locate from Results. All posteriors re-verified: CTLA4 0.201 BBJ (H3 0.799) / 0.953 UKB / 0.978 FinnGen; TNFSF14 0.994 BBJ and 0.017 FinnGen; IFNGR1 0.989 and 0.020; the 16p11.2 trio 0.636/0.388/0.168 in BBJ with a maximum of 0.115 across UKB and FinnGen; MAPKAPK5 0.000 BBJ. No displayed value changed.
revision_note_20260915_results_robustnes: Robustness subsection: two redundancies removed and two numbers added. The sentence 'This distinguished stability to the frequency substitution from sensitivity to the assumed prior...' restated the two sentences before it; replaced by one clause carrying the same principle. Three consecutive caveats about the detection benchmarks were merged to two. Verified against Supplementary Data 3: TSHR BBJ 0.951/0.907/0.661 and FinnGen 0.986/0.972/0.875 across p12 = 1e-5/5e-6/1e-6. revision_note_20260915_discussion_p1p2: Discussion opening: the claim of stronger TSHR evidence was stated for 'the same outcomes' without scope, but in UKB IGF1R's shared-variant support (0.404) exceeds TSHR's (0.226) -- both below 0.80 -- while Results and Conclusions had both scoped the claim to BBJ and FinnGen. The paragraph now states that in UKB neither gene reached the threshold, closing the gap a reader would find in Table 2. On author request it also states the direction of the TSHR association (higher genetically proxied expression, lower odds) and what the FinnGen recovery means for TED: the signal extends to a TED-enriched population but, because that outcome uses population controls, does not isolate eye-disease susceptibility within GD. Dropped a sentence that only described Figures 1-3. In the second paragraph, 'Experimental receptor crosstalk [5] and tissue-specific regulation [29] provide complementary biological context' asserted relevance without stating it; the two citations now carry the premises the following hypothesis rests on (receptors physically scaffolded; regulation tissue-dependent). Citation-claim mapping unchanged. Verified MR P values: TSHR beats IGF1R in all three outcomes (1.09e-14 vs 0.0212; 8.77e-28 vs 0.0117; 2.82e-07 vs 0.182), so the MR half of the claim needed no scoping.
revision_note_20260915_discussion_p3p4: Discussion paragraphs 3-4. Paragraph 3: the variant behind the scale comparison was unnamed and the two numbers were juxtaposed without the mechanism joining them. It is rs179252, and the link is exact -- per major_review_evidence.json the variant shifts reconstructed expression by 0.10546 SD, and variant log OR / 0.10546 reproduces the MR beta to 1e-4 in all three outcomes (-0.22103/0.10546 = -2.09595 BBJ; -0.25691 = -2.43623 UKB; -0.24587 = -2.33149 FinnGen). The text now states that the larger MR estimates follow from the scale, not from a larger effect, which pre-empts the obvious objection that OR 0.12 is implausible. Variant ORs 0.8017/0.7734/0.7820 displayed as 0.80/0.77/0.78, verified. Two sentences both saying the thymic step is unproven were merged. Paragraph 4: the single-causal-variant constraint was stated four times; the pure restatement ('These findings are therefore interpreted within the single-causal-variant model') removed, and 'fitted' no longer appears in two consecutive sentences.
revision_note_20260915_discussion_p5p6: Discussion paragraphs 5-6. Verified: seven of nine FinnGen loci are H2-dominant (IGF1R, TNFSF14, IFNGR1, MAPKAPK5, HSD3B7, VKORC1, PRSS36; not TSHR or CTLA4). Paragraph 6's closing restated the Results Robustness closing almost in function -- both said the benchmarks measure precision and cannot separate absence from low power -- so 42 words were compressed to 27 while keeping the distinction. OPEN ITEM for the authors, not changed here: the citation [9, 10] on 'Significant associations such as TNFSF14 and IFNGR1 remain relevant to follow-up'. Ji et al. [9] does support IFNGR1 -- published summaries list it among genes positively associated with GD risk and among putative causal genes, alongside TSHR -- but lists TNFSF13, not TNFSF14. Li et al. [10] is a gut-microbiota-to-inflammatory-protein mediation study of Graves ophthalmopathy (FinnGen 691 cases, a different release from the 858 used here) and does not appear to report either gene. Verified from search summaries only; nature.com and PMC are blocked from this environment, so the papers themselves were not read.
revision_note_20260916_discussion_p7_lim: Discussion paragraph 7 and Limitations. Three corrections. (1) 'Similar effects in two population-control GWAS would not by themselves resolve this issue because the phenotypes and participants can overlap' -- UKB and FinnGen draw from different national biobanks, so their participants do not meaningfully overlap; the real argument is that both use population controls rather than GD patients without eye disease, and that a Graves ophthalmopathy case is by definition also a GD case. Rewritten to say that. (2) 'the UKB TSHR and BBJ CTLA4 discordances remain unresolved by a multi-signal model' read as though a multi-signal model had been fitted and failed, one sentence after stating it was not evaluated; now 'Without such a model, ... remain unresolved'. The same phrase in Discussion paragraph 4 italicises both genes and this one did not -- the only genuine gene-italic defect in the main text. (3) The two unspaced em-dashes in 'observations-four TED samples and one control-remain' were the only ones in the main text against 13 spaced; now 15 spaced, 0 unspaced. Audited gene italics across Introduction-Discussion: the remaining bare occurrences are correct -- 'TSHR and IGF-1R interact' and 'recognition of TSHR as self' are the PROTEIN, and '### TSHR', '### IGF1R', '### CTLA4' are subsection headings, all deliberately unitalicised.
